html:
A large group of Germanic peoples first described by Julius Caesar, one branch of which founded a kingdom in northwest Spain. The map shows that kingdom in 500, in Gallaecia, now Galicia and northern Portugal.

In the 1st century BCE the Suebi lived east of the Rhine, and Roman writers used the name for many peoples of inner Germany. At the end of 406 a band of Suebi crossed the Rhine with the Vandals and Alans, and in 409 they reached Spain. In Gallaecia they founded a kingdom with its capital at Braga, one of the first barbarian kingdoms inside the western empire. Their king Rechiar became a Catholic around 448, early for a Germanic ruler.

The Visigoths beat them in 456 and the kingdom shrank to the northwest. In the 6th century the bishop Martin of Braga brought them back to Catholic Christianity. In 585 the Visigothic king Leovigild conquered them and made their land part of the Visigothic Kingdom.
sum: A large group of Germanic peoples first described by Julius Caesar, one branch of which founded a kingdom in northwest Spain. The map shows that kingdom in 500, in Gallaecia, now Galicia and northern Portugal.
